name: Java
description: Java is a strongly typed, object-oriented language used for Android apps, enterprise systems and university courses.

blocks.html:
Introduction to Java

What is Java?

Java is a powerful, object-oriented language used for Android apps, enterprise back-ends, banking systems and big universities' courses. It is strongly typed: every variable has a declared type, and the compiler catches many mistakes before the program runs.

  • JDK (Java Development Kit): tools to write and compile code.
  • JVM (Java Virtual Machine): runs the compiled code, so the same program works on Windows, Mac and Linux ("write once, run anywhere").
  • Source files end in .java; the compiler turns them into .class files (bytecode).

Why Java? Where is it Used?

  • Object-oriented: programs are built from classes and objects.
  • Platform independent: compiled once, runs on any computer with a JVM.
  • Safe and robust: strong typing, exceptions and automatic memory cleanup (garbage collection).
  • Huge ecosystem: libraries, tools and a very large community.
  • Fast: the JVM optimises hot code while the program runs.
AreaExamples
Android appsMany Android apps are written in Java or Kotlin
Enterprise back-endsSpring Boot services in banks, telecoms and e-commerce
Big dataHadoop, Spark and Kafka run on the JVM
Games and toolsMinecraft, IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse
UniversitiesA very common first object-oriented language

JDK, JRE and JVM

NameWhat it isWho needs it
JDKDevelopment Kit: compiler javac, tools and the runtimeYou, as a developer
JRERuntime Environment: the JVM plus standard librariesAnyone who only runs Java programs
JVMThe virtual machine that runs bytecodeIncluded in the JDK and JRE

The journey of a Java program:

  1. You write Main.java (source code).
  2. The compiler javac Main.java creates Main.class (bytecode).
  3. The JVM runs it with java Main, translating bytecode for your computer.

Installing Java and Choosing a Tool

Install a JDK (version 17 or 21 are long-term-support releases, good for learning), for example from adoptium.net or oracle.com/java. Then check it in a terminal:

java -version
javac -version

If javac is not found, add the JDK bin folder to your PATH (and set JAVA_HOME). Then pick a tool to write code:

ToolNotes
IntelliJ IDEA CommunityMost popular Java IDE, free
VS Code + Extension Pack for JavaLight and fast, good for beginners
Eclipse / NetBeansFree IDEs often used in universities
Online compilersQuick practice without installing anything

Common Beginner Errors

Read the compiler message: it names the file, the line number and the problem.

MessageUsual cause and fix
';' expectedA semicolon is missing at the end of a statement.
class Main is public, should be declared in a file named Main.javaThe file name must match the public class name.
cannot find symbolA name is misspelled, not declared, or an import is missing.
incompatible types: possible lossy conversion from double to intYou are storing a decimal in an int. Use a cast or a double.
Could not find or load main classWrong class name or folder when running java.
missing return statementA method with a return type does not return on every path.

Practice Time

  1. Install the JDK and run java -version and javac -version.
  2. Write a program that prints your name, roll number and university on three lines.
  3. Use printf to print Total: 250.50 with two decimals.
  4. Remove a semicolon on purpose and read the compiler error.
  5. Compile and run the same program from the terminal with javac and java.

Quick Summary

  • Java is strongly typed and object-oriented; code is compiled to bytecode and run by the JVM.
  • JDK = tools to develop, JRE = runtime, JVM = the machine that runs bytecode.
  • A program starts in public static void main(String[] args).
  • Statements end with ;, blocks use { }, names are case sensitive.
  • Read compiler errors: the line number and the message tell you what to fix.

Variables & Data Types

Declaring Variables

In Java you write the type first, then the name. Once declared, a variable can only hold that type.

Ayesha is 20 years old
Grade A, student: true
39.98
100

blocks.html:
• final makes a constant that cannot change.
  • String starts with a capital S: it is a class, not a primitive.
  • Characters use single quotes ('A'), strings use double quotes.

Primitive Types

TypeSizeHoldsExample
byte1 byteTiny whole numbers (-128 to 127)100
short2 bytesSmall whole numbers (about +-32,000)30000
int4 bytesWhole numbers (about +-2 billion)42
long8 bytesVery big whole numbers9000000000L
float4 bytesDecimal numbers (about 7 digits)3.14f
double8 bytesDecimal numbers (about 15 digits)3.14
boolean1 bit of informationtrue or falsetrue
char2 bytesOne character (Unicode)'A'

Use int for whole numbers and double for decimals unless you have a reason to use another type. String is not a primitive; it is a class.

Naming Rules and Style

RuleValidInvalid
Letters, digits, _ and $ onlytotal_1, $pricemy-name, a b
Cannot start with a digititem22item
Cannot be a keywordcountclass, int, static
Case sensitiveage and Age are different
  • Style: variables in camelCase (studentName), constants in UPPER_CASE (MAX_MARKS).
  • Choose meaningful names: totalMarks is better than tm.

Type Casting and Integer Division

Java converts a smaller type to a bigger one automatically (int to double). Going the other way needs an explicit cast. Dividing two ints gives an int.
Widening order: byte to short to int to long to float to double. Moving right is automatic; moving left needs a cast and may lose data.
Overflow, Precision and char Arithmetic

• An int that goes past its maximum wraps around silently. Use long for big values.
  • double stores approximations: for money, use BigDecimal or whole cents in a long.
  • A char is really a number (its Unicode code), so 'a' + 1 is the number 98.
var, Constants and Scope

• var lets the compiler work out the type, but it still has one fixed type.
  • A variable lives only inside the { } block where it was declared (its scope).
  • A final variable can be assigned only once.

Default Values and Wrapper Classes

Fields (variables of a class) get default values. Local variables inside methods get none: you must give them a value before use. Every primitive also has a wrapper class (Integer, Double, Boolean, Character...) used with collections.

PrimitiveWrapperDefault field value
intInteger0
doubleDouble0.0
booleanBooleanfalse
charCharacter'\u0000' (empty char)
String / objectsthe class itselfnull

Common Mistakes

  • Writing int x = 3.5; (a decimal does not fit an int). Use double or cast.
  • Using a local variable before giving it a value.
  • Forgetting L on a big literal: long n = 3000000000; fails, 3000000000L works.
  • Using "A" (a String) where 'A' (a char) is needed.
  • Declaring the same variable name twice in the same scope.

Practice Time

  1. Declare variables for a student (name, age, GPA, enrolled) and print one sentence.
  2. Store 7 and 2 in int variables and print the sum, the integer division and the exact division.
  3. Convert 36.6 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit with double variables.
  4. Show what happens when you add 1 to Integer.MAX_VALUE.
  5. Print the character that comes after 'K' in the alphabet.

Quick Summary

  • Type first, then name: int age = 20;.
  • Eight primitive types; String is a class.
  • Widening is automatic; narrowing needs a cast.
  • final makes constants; var infers the type.
  • Fields get default values, local variables do not.

Input, Output & Math

Printing with printf and String.format

printf and String.format use format specifiers: a % sign followed by a letter. %n is a portable new line.

%fDecimal number%.2f keeps 2 decimals

Reading Input with Scanner

A Scanner reads text from the keyboard (System.in), a string or a file. This is the usual program that asks the user for values:

import java.util.Scanner;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in);
        System.out.print("Your name: ");
        String name = in.nextLine();
        System.out.print("Your age: ");
        int age = in.nextInt();
        System.out.println("Hello " + name + ", next year you will be " + (age + 1));
        in.close();
    }
}
The next demo reads from a fixed text instead of the keyboard, so you can see exactly what each method does:

Classic trap: after nextInt() the Enter key is still waiting in the input. Call in.nextLine() once to remove it before you read a full line.

Common Mistakes

  • Calling nextLine() right after nextInt() and getting an empty line (see the trap above).
  • Forgetting import java.util.Scanner;.
  • Using %d with a double (it throws IllegalFormatConversionException).
  • Forgetting %n or \n in printf: it does not add a new line by itself.
  • Closing Scanner(System.in) and then trying to read again.

Practice Time

  1. Ask for two numbers and print their sum, product and average with 2 decimals.
  2. Ask for a radius and print the area and circumference of a circle.
  3. Print a price list as an aligned table using printf and %-10s, %8.2f.
  4. Simulate rolling two dice with Random and print the total.
  5. Ask for a number as text, convert it, and handle a bad input with try/catch.

Quick Summary

  • printf / String.format format output with %d, %f, %s, %n.
  • Scanner reads keyboard input; clear the leftover newline after nextInt().
  • Math provides pow, sqrt, abs, round, max, min and more.
  • Random makes random numbers; a seed repeats them.
  • Integer.parseInt and String.valueOf convert between text and numbers.

Common Mistakes

  • Using = instead of == in a condition (assign versus compare).
  • Comparing Strings with == instead of .equals().
  • A semicolon right after if (...): if (x > 5); ends the if with an empty statement.
  • Forgetting break in an old-style switch.
  • Writing 1 < x < 10: Java needs x > 1 && x < 10.
  • Integer division surprises: 1 / 2 is 0.

Practice Time

  1. Given a number, print whether it is positive, negative or zero.
  2. Convert marks to a grade (A, B, C, D, F) with if / else if.
  3. Given a day number 1-7, print the name of the day using switch.
  4. Check whether a year is a leap year.
  5. Print the largest of three numbers without using Math.max.

Quick Summary

  • Comparison operators give boolean; combine with &&, ||, !.
  • && and || short-circuit: the second part may be skipped.
  • Compare numbers with ==, Strings with .equals().
  • switch (arrow style) is clean; yield returns a value from a block.
  • The ternary ? : is a short if/else for values.

Loops

for, while and do-while

LoopUse it when
forYou know how many times
whileYou repeat until a condition changes
do-whileThe body must run at least once

for round 3

blocks.html: A for header has three parts: start, condition, step: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++). The loop variable i exists only inside the loop.

Enhanced for, break and continue

  • The enhanced for loop visits every item of an array or collection.
  • break exits the loop; continue skips to the next round.

blocks.output: Sum of small even numbers: 28

blocks.html: Nested Loops
The inner loop runs completely for each round of the outer loop.
Pattern Printing
For patterns, think in rows and columns: the outer loop is the row, the inner loop prints that row.
Labeled break and continue
A label (outer:) lets break or continue act on an outer loop. Use it rarely; it can make code harder to read.
Common Loop Patterns

blocks.html: while Loops with Digits

blocks.output:
Digit sum: 15
Reversed: 4321
stopped at 3

blocks.html: n % 10 gives the last digit and n / 10 removes it. This idea solves many number problems.

Infinite Loops and Input Menus

A menu usually runs inside do-while or while (true) until the user chooses to exit:

Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in);
int choice;
do {
    System.out.println("1) Say hello   2) Say bye   0) Exit");
    choice = in.nextInt();
    if (choice == 1) System.out.println("Hello!");
    else if (choice == 2) System.out.println("Bye!");
} while (choice != 0);
  • If a loop never ends, press Ctrl + C in the terminal to stop it.
  • Make sure something inside the loop moves the condition toward false.

Common Mistakes

  • Off-by-one errors: i <= n versus i < n.
  • A semicolon after the loop header: for (...); runs an empty loop.
  • Forgetting to change the variable in a while loop (endless loop).
  • Using == with Strings in a loop condition (use .equals()).
  • Changing a collection while looping over it (ConcurrentModificationException).

Practice Time

  1. Print the multiplication table of a number up to 10.
  2. Print the sum of all numbers from 1 to 100 and of all even numbers from 1 to 100.
  3. Print the first 10 Fibonacci numbers.
  4. Print all prime numbers below 50.
  5. Print a number pyramid for n = 5 using nested loops.

Quick Summary

  • for when you know the count, while for a condition, do-while to run at least once.
  • The enhanced for loop (for (int x : arr)) is the easiest way to read every item.
  • break leaves a loop, continue skips a round; labels reach outer loops.
  • Nested loops build tables and patterns.
  • n % 10 and n / 10 extract and remove digits.

Arrays & Strings

Arrays

An array holds a fixed number of values of the same type. The size cannot change after creation, and indexes start at 0.

StringBuilder: Changing Text Efficiently

Because a String never changes, joining text in a loop creates many temporary objects. A StringBuilder is a changeable text buffer that is much faster for building text.

Common Mistakes

  • Using == to compare Strings. Use .equals().
  • Using length for arrays and length() for Strings: arrays have a field, strings have a method.
  • Expecting s.toUpperCase() to change s: Strings are immutable, assign the result.
  • Index out of range: valid array indexes are 0 to length - 1.
  • Thinking int[] b = a; copies an array (it only copies the reference). Use Arrays.copyOf.
  • Joining many strings with + inside a big loop. Use StringBuilder.

Practice Time

  1. Store 5 marks in an array and print the total, average, highest and lowest.
  2. Reverse an array without creating a second array.
  3. Count how many times a character appears in a sentence.
  4. Check whether two words are anagrams (use toCharArray and Arrays.sort).
  5. Print a 3 x 3 matrix and the sum of its diagonal.

Quick Summary

  • Arrays have a fixed size, start at index 0, and length is a field.
  • Use java.util.Arrays for sort, toString, copyOf, fill, equals.
  • 2D arrays are arrays of arrays; rows may have different lengths.
  • Strings are immutable: methods return new strings.
  • Use StringBuilder to build or change text efficiently.

Methods

Writing Methods

A method is a named block of code. Its header says who can call it, whether it belongs to the class (static), what it returns and what it takes.

public static int add(int a, int b) {
    return a + b;
}

blocks.output:
5
true false
Hello, Ali

blocks.html:
• void means the method returns nothing.
  • Parameters are a copy of the values you pass: Java is pass-by-value.

Overloading

You can have several methods with the same name if their parameters differ. This is called overloading.
Java picks the version that matches the number and types of the arguments. The return type alone cannot tell overloads apart.

Pass by Value

Changing a primitive parameter inside a method does not change the caller's variable. (For arrays and objects the reference is copied, so changes to the contents are visible.)
Varargs, Arrays and Early Return

static vs Instance Methods

static methodinstance method
Belongs toThe classEach object
Called withClassName.method()object.method()
Can use fields of the object?NoYes (this)

Recursion

A method can call itself. Every recursive method needs a base case (when to stop) and a step that moves toward it.

blocks.output:

3
2

Go!
Too deep: a base case is missing

blocks.html: Without a base case Java throws StackOverflowError. For simple counting, a loop is usually faster and safer.

Writing Good Methods

  • Use a verb name in camelCase: calculateTotal, isValid.
  • Make each method do one job; if it is long, split it.
  • Prefer return over printing inside a method, so the result can be reused.
  • Keep the number of parameters small (three or fewer is a good habit).
  • Add a Javadoc comment (/** ... */) for public methods.

Common Mistakes

  • Forgetting return in a method that has a return type (missing return statement).
  • Calling an instance method from main without creating an object.
  • Expecting a method to change a primitive argument.
  • Using the same name and parameters twice (not a valid overload).
  • Recursion without a base case.

Practice Time

  1. Write isEven(int n) and isPositive(int n).
  2. Write average(int... numbers) that works for any count.
  3. Write reverse(String s) that returns the reversed text.
  4. Write a recursive method that adds the digits of a number.
  5. Write overloaded area methods for a square, a rectangle and a circle.

Quick Summary

  • A method has a header (modifiers, return type, name, parameters) and a body.
  • Overloading means the same name with different parameters.
  • Java is pass-by-value; objects and arrays pass a copy of the reference.
  • static methods belong to the class; instance methods need an object.
  • Recursion needs a base case.

Classes & Objects

Classes, Objects and Constructors

A class is a blueprint with fields (data) and methods (actions). new creates an object, and the constructor sets it up. this means the current object.

• If you write no constructor, Java gives you an empty default one. Once you write one, the default disappears.
  • this(...) calls another constructor of the same class (it must be the first line).
  • A variable of a class type holds a reference. null means "no object": using it causes NullPointerException.
  • toString() decides what System.out.println(object) shows.

Encapsulation

Make fields private and give controlled access through public getters and setters. This lets the class protect its own rules.

ModifierVisible from

Getters, Setters and Validation

blocks.html: A setter is a good place for validation: the object can never end up with invalid data. An array of objects works like any other array.

static Members

A static field or method belongs to the class, not to a single object. All objects share it.

blocks.output:
Objects created: 3
Counter class

blocks.html: Use static for shared counters, constants (static final) and helper methods that do not need an object.

Common Mistakes

  • Forgetting new: Student s; creates only a variable, not an object.
  • Using an object variable that is still null (NullPointerException).
  • Writing name = name; in a constructor instead of this.name = name;.
  • Making every field public instead of private with getters and setters.
  • Comparing objects with == when you mean equals().

Practice Time

  1. Create a Rectangle class with width and height and methods area() and perimeter().
  2. Create a BankAccount with private balance, deposit, withdraw and getBalance.
  3. Create a Student class with validation and a toString() method, and store 5 students in an array.
  4. Add a static counter that tells how many Student objects were created.
  5. Create a Car class with two constructors, one of which calls the other with this(...).

Quick Summary

  • A class is a blueprint; new makes an object; the constructor initialises it.
  • this refers to the current object.
  • Use private fields with getters and setters (encapsulation).
  • static members belong to the class and are shared.
  • Object variables hold references; null means no object.

Inheritance & Interfaces

Inheritance

A class can extend another to reuse its fields and methods. The child may override a method (mark it with @Override) and calls the parent's constructor with super(...). Java allows only one parent class.

• The parent constructor runs first (super(...) must be the first line of the child constructor).
  • protected fields can be used by subclasses.
  • super.method() calls the parent's version of a method.
  • instanceof checks the real type of an object; instanceof Manager mgr also gives you a typed variable.
  • A class marked final cannot be extended; a final method cannot be overridden.

Polymorphism and Abstract Classes

A parent variable can hold any child object, and Java runs the child's version of the method. An abstract class cannot be instantiated; it forces children to implement its abstract methods.

Interfaces

An interface is a contract: it lists methods a class promises to have. A class can implement many interfaces.

abstract classinterface
Can have fields and constructorsYesNo (only constants)
A class can useOne (extends)Many (implements)
Best forA shared base with some codeA capability (Comparable, Runnable)
Default and Static Methods in Interfaces

blocks.output:
Duck flies
Duck swims
I can fly
1000

blocks.html: Since Java 8 an interface may have default methods (with a body) and static methods. Interface methods are public automatically, so the implementing class must write public.

Inheritance or Composition?

Use inheritance for an "is a" relationship (a Dog is an Animal). Use composition for a "has a" relationship (a Car has an Engine): keep one object as a field inside another.

blocks.output: Toyota: Engine started

blocks.html: Prefer composition when you only want to reuse behaviour. Inheritance ties child and parent tightly together.

Common Mistakes

  • Forgetting to call super(...) when the parent has no default constructor.
  • Overloading by accident instead of overriding: always add @Override so the compiler checks you.
  • Weaker access when overriding (public method cannot become package-private).
  • Trying to create an object of an abstract class or an interface.
  • Forgetting the word public on methods that implement an interface.

Practice Time

  1. Create Vehicle, then Car and Bike that extend it and override describe().
  2. Create an abstract Shape with area(), and Rectangle and Circle subclasses; store them in one array.
  3. Create an interface Printable and implement it in two unrelated classes.
  4. Build Employee and Manager where Manager adds a bonus and overrides annualPay().
  5. Model a Library that has a list of Book objects (composition).

Quick Summary

  • extends reuses a parent class (only one); implements signs one or more interfaces.
  • @Override replaces a parent method; super reaches the parent.
  • Polymorphism: a parent-type variable runs the child's method.
  • Abstract classes share code; interfaces describe capabilities.
  • Prefer composition for "has a" relationships.

More Object-Oriented Java

The Object Class: toString, equals, hashCode

Every class in Java inherits from Object. Three methods are worth overriding: toString() (readable text), equals() (when are two objects equal?) and hashCode() (must match equals, used by HashMap and HashSet).

blocks.html: Rule: if two objects are equals, they must return the same hashCode. Otherwise collections such as HashSet will misbehave.

Enums

An enum is a fixed set of named constants (days, levels, directions). Enums can hold fields and methods and work nicely in switch.

Records (Java 16+)

A record is a short way to write a class that only carries data. Java writes the constructor, getters, equals, hashCode and toString for you. Records are immutable.

Pattern Matching and Sealed Types (Java 17-21)

Modern Java adds instanceof patterns, switch patterns and sealed types that list all allowed subtypes. The compiler then checks that your switch covers every case.

Packages, Imports and final

A package is a folder-like group of classes. The first line of a file names its package. Use import to reach classes from other packages.

package com.learninghub.app;          // the first line of the file

import java.util.List;               // one class
import java.util.*;                  // everything in java.util
import static java.lang.Math.sqrt;   // a static member

public class Main { ... }
Keyword on...Meaning
a variableCan be assigned only once (a constant)
a methodCannot be overridden by a subclass
a classCannot be extended (String is final)

java.lang (String, Math, Integer...) is imported automatically. An immutable class has only private final fields and no setters; String and records work this way.

The SOLID Habits (Short Version)

HabitMeaning in plain words
Single responsibilityA class should have one reason to change
Open / closedAdd new behaviour by adding new classes, not by editing old ones
Program to an interfaceDeclare List<String> x = new ArrayList<>();, not ArrayList<String> x
Favour compositionUse "has a" before "is a"
Hide dataPrivate fields, public methods

Common Mistakes

  • Overriding equals but not hashCode.
  • Comparing enum values with equals in a way that causes NullPointerException (use ==).
  • Using an inner class from static main without creating an outer object.
  • Trying to modify a record field (records are immutable).
  • Using a switch pattern with a Java version older than 21.

Practice Time

  1. Create a Person class with equals and hashCode on name and age, and put two equal persons in a HashSet.
  2. Create an enum Planet with mass and radius and a method that returns the surface gravity.
  3. Replace a plain data class of yours with a record.
  4. Write a sealed interface Vehicle with Car, Bike records and a switch that returns the number of wheels.
  5. Create an anonymous class and then rewrite it as a lambda.

Quick Summary

  • Every class extends Object; override toString, equals and hashCode together.
  • Enums are fixed sets of constants that can have fields and methods.
  • Records are compact immutable data classes.
  • Nested, inner, anonymous classes and lambdas keep small code close to where it is used.
  • Packages organise code; final prevents change.

Exceptions & Collections

Exceptions

Errors in Java are exceptions. Handle them with try, catch and finally. Checked exceptions (like IOException) must be handled or declared with throws; unchecked ones (like NullPointerException) need not.

Use throw to create your own exception.

Java has a hierarchy of exception classes. Exception is the base class for checked exceptions, and RuntimeException is the base for unchecked ones.

Common Mistakes

  • Catching Exception everywhere and hiding real bugs.
  • An empty catch block: at least print the message or log it.
  • Using primitives in generics: List<int> is not allowed. Use List<Integer>.
  • Calling list.remove(5) on List<Integer> and removing the item at index 5 by accident.
  • Modifying a list while looping over it with a for-each loop.
  • Forgetting import java.util.*;.

  1. Ask for a number and keep asking until the user types a valid integer (try/catch in a loop).

Quick Summary

  • try / catch / finally handle errors; try-with-resources closes things automatically.
  • Checked exceptions need throws or catch; unchecked ones do not.
  • ArrayList is a resizable list (add, get, remove, size).

  • Declare collections with the interface type and a generic type argument.

Common Mistakes

  • Using a List and checking contains in a loop when a HashSet would be much faster.
  • Putting objects in a HashSet or as HashMap keys without equals and hashCode.

Quick Summary

  • HashSet / TreeSet / LinkedHashSet differ in ordering and speed.

  • Comparable is the natural order; Comparator is any custom order.
  • Use Iterator.remove or removeIf to delete while looping.

Generics, Lambdas & Streams

Generics

Generics let you write one class or method that works with many types, while the compiler still checks the types. List<String> is a generic type; T below is a type parameter.

HELLO 43
9 pear
age=20

blocks.html:
• Type parameters use one capital letter by convention: T (type), E (element), K / V (key / value).
  • <T extends Comparable<T>> is a bound: T must be comparable.
  • ? extends Number is a wildcard: a list of Number or any subtype.
  • Generics only work with objects, so use Integer, not int.

Lambdas and Functional Interfaces

A lambda is a short anonymous function: (parameters) -> result. It can be used wherever an interface with a single abstract method (a functional interface) is expected.

A method reference such as String::toUpperCase or System.out::println is a shorter form of a lambda that only calls one method.

Streams

A stream processes a collection step by step: source, then intermediate steps (filter, map, sorted), then one terminal step (collect, sum, forEach). Streams do not change the original list.

Optional

Optional<T> is a box that may or may not hold a value. It is a safer way to say "there might be no result" than returning null.

blocks.output:
JAVA default false
nothing here

blocks.html: Avoid optional.get() without checking. Prefer orElse, map, ifPresent and orElseThrow.

Common Mistakes

  • Using primitives as type arguments: List<int> does not compile.
  • Reusing a stream: a stream can be consumed only once.
  • Changing outside variables inside a lambda (they must be effectively final).
  • Long chains of stream steps that nobody can read. A simple loop is fine sometimes.
  • Calling Optional.get() on an empty Optional (throws NoSuchElementException).

Practice Time

  1. Write a generic method swap(T[] array, int i, int j).
  2. Use a Predicate<Integer> to keep only the even numbers of a list.
  3. Use streams to print the squares of the odd numbers from 1 to 10.
  4. Group a list of words by length with Collectors.groupingBy.
  5. From a list of students, print the name of the student with the highest marks using max and Optional.

Quick Summary

  • Generics give type safety with reusable classes and methods.
  • A lambda is a short function for a one-method (functional) interface.
  • Streams: source, intermediate steps, one terminal step.
  • Optional represents "maybe no value" without null.
  • Method references (Class::method) shorten simple lambdas.

• Path.of("a", "b") builds a path that works on Windows, Mac and Linux.
  • dir.resolve("a.txt") appends a name to a folder path.
  • Files.list shows one folder; Files.walk goes through all sub-folders. Close the stream with try-with-resources.

Common Mistakes

  • Forgetting to handle or declare IOException (the compiler will insist).
  • Writing with writeString and expecting it to add to the file: it replaces unless you pass StandardOpenOption.APPEND.
  • Not closing readers and writers. Always use try-with-resources.
  • Hard-coding Windows paths like "C:\\files\\a.txt". Use Path.of and relative paths.
  • Reading a huge file with readAllLines: read line by line instead.

Practice Time

  1. Write names typed by the user into names.txt, one per line, then read the file back.
  2. Count the lines and the words in a text file.
  3. Copy one file to another using Files.copy and print the size of both.
  4. Read a CSV file of marks and print the average and the highest mark.
  5. Handle a missing file by printing a friendly message and asking for another file name.

Quick Summary

  • Path is a location; Files does the reading, writing and managing.
  • Use BufferedReader / BufferedWriter for line-by-line work on big files.
  • File methods throw the checked IOException: catch it or declare throws.
  • Always use try-with-resources so files are closed.
  • Files.list and Files.walk explore folders.
